quote: As the Creator and Preserver of men, Thou art gloriously manifest; but O! how much more gloriously art Thou revealed as reconciling ungrateful enemies to Thyself by the blood of Thy eternal Son. Here Thy beneficence displays its brightest splendor; here Thou dost fully display Thy most magnificent titles; The Lord, the Lord God , merciful and gracious , long-suffering and abundant in goodness. How unsearchable are Thy ways, and Thy paths past finding out!
author: Elizabeth Rowe
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: If I were to live to the world's end, and do all the good that man can do, I must still cry, "Mercy!" Why then should I be unwilling or afraid to die this moment, with a sense of God's pardoning love, when I can have no other claim to salvation if I were to live forever?
author: Thomas Adams
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Depth of mercy!—can there be 
Mercy still reserved for me? 
Can my God His wrath forbear? 
Me, the chief of sinners, spare?
author: Charles Wesley
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: God's mercy is a holy mercy, which knows how to pardon sin, not to protect it; it is a sanctuary for the penitent, not for the presumptuous.
author: Bishop Reynolds
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: And now we beseech of Thee that we may have every day some such sense of God's mercy and of the power of God about us, as we have of the fullness of the light of heaven before us.
author: H. W. Beecher
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It is as easy for God to supply thy greatest as thy smallest wants, even as it was within His power to form a system or an atom, to create a blazing sun as to kindle the fire-fly's lamp.
author: Thomas Guthrie
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It is impossible for the mind which is not totally destitute of piety, to behold the sublime, the awful, the amazing works of creation and providence—the heavens with their luminaries, the mountains, the ocean, the storm, the earthquake, the volcano, the circuit of the seasons, and the revolutions of empires—without marking in them all the mighty hand of God, and feeling strong emotions of reverence toward the Author of these stupendous works.
author: Timothy Dwight
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The same Being that fashioned the insect, whose existence is only discerned by a microscope, and gave that invisible speck a system of ducts and other organs to perform its vital functions, created the enormous mass of the planet thirteen hundred times larger than our earth, and launched it in its course round the sun, and the comet, wheeling with a velocity that would carry it round our globe in less than two minutes of time, and yet revolving through so prodigious a space that it takes near six centuries to encircle the sun!
author: Lord Brougham
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There is nothing left to us but to see how we may be approved of Him, and how we may roll the weight of our weak souls in well-doing upon Him, who is God omnipotent.
author: Rutherford
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Oh, when His wisdom can mistake, 
His might decay, His love forsake, 
Then may His children cease to sing,— 
"The Lord omnipotent is King!"
author: Conder
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: God is everywhere present by His power. He rolls the orb of heaven with His hand; He fixes the earth with His foot. He guides all creatures with His eye, and refreshes them with His influence; He makes the powers of hell to shake with His terrors, and binds the devils with His word.
author: Jeremy Taylor
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There are regions beyond the most nebulous outskirts of matter; but no regions beyond the Divine goodness. We may conceive of tracts where there are no worlds, but not of any where there is no God of mercy.
author: J. W. Alexander
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
He knoweth all; the end 
Is clear as the beginning to His eye; 
Then wait in peace, secure though storms roll by, 
 He knoweth all, O friend!
author: Sunday School Times
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: What must be the knowledge of Him, from whom all created minds have derived both their power of knowledge, and the innumerable objects of their knowledge! What must be the wisdom of Him, from whom all things derive their wisdom!
author: Timothy Dwight
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: However dark our lot may be, there is light enough on the other side of the cloud, in that pure empyrean where God dwells, to irradiate every darkness of this world; light enough to clear every difficult question, remove every ground of obscurity, conquer every atheistic suspicion, silence every hard judgment, light enough to satisfy, nay, to ravish the mind forever.
author: Horace Bushnell
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: He who cannot see the workings of a Divine wisdom in the order of the heavens, the change of the seasons, the flowing of the tides, the operations of the wind and other elements, the structure of the human body, the circulation of the blood through a variety of vessels wonderfully arranged and conducted, the instinct of beasts, their tempers and dispositions, the growth of plants, and their many effects for meat and medicine; he who cannot see all these and many other things as the evident contrivance of a Divine wisdom is sottishly blind, and unworthy the name of man.
author: William Jones of Nayland
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The wisdom of the Lord is infinite as are also His glory and His power. Ye heavens, sing His praises; sun, moon, and planets, glorify Him in your ineffable language! Praise Him, celestial harmonies, and all ye who can comprehend them! And thou, my soul, praise thy Creator! It is by Him and in Him that all exist.
author: Kepler
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It is certain that this is not only good which the Almighty has done, but that it is best; He hath reckoned all your steps to heaven.
author: Rutherford
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Let us ask ourselves seriously and honestly, "What do I believe after all? What manner of man am I after all? What sort of show would I make after all, if the people around me knew my heart and all my secret thoughts?" What sort of show then do I already make in the sight of Almighty God, who sees every man exactly as he is?
author: Charles Kingsley
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Take comfort, and recollect however little you and I may know, God knows; He knows Himself and you and me and all things; and His mercy is over all His works.
author: Charles Kingsley
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
I need Thy presence every passing hour; 
What, but Thy grace, can foil the tempter's power? 
Who, like Thyself, my guide and stay can be? 
Through cloud and sunshine, oh, abide with me!
author: H. F. Lyte
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The presence of God calms the soul, and gives it quiet and repose.
author: Fenelon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Life should be a constant vision of God's presence. Here is our defense against being led away by the gauds and shows of earth's vulgar attractions.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The never-ceasing boom of the great ocean as it breaks on the beach, drowns all smaller sounds.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Do we vividly feel that He is near us as our everlasting Friend, to guide, cheer, and bless our aspirations and our efforts? And in this confidence do we watch, pray, strive, press forward, and seek resolutely for ourselves and fellow-beings the highest end of existence, even the perfection of our immortal souls?
author: W. E. Channing
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: He who knows what it is to enjoy God will dread His loss; he who has seen His face will fear to see His back.
author: Richard Alleine
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: I know that as night and shadows are good for flowers, and moonlight and dews are better than a continual sun, so is Christ's absence of special use, and that it hath some nourishing virtue in it, and giveth sap to humility, and putteth an edge on hunger, and furnisheth a fair field for faith to put forth itself.
author: Rutherford
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The vision of the Divine presence ever takes the form which our circumstances most require.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: As the soul is the life of the body, so God is the life of the soul. As therefore the body perishes when the soul leaves it, so the soul dies when God departs from it.
author: St. Augustine
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We may search long to find where God is, but we shall find Him in those who keep the words of Christ. For the Lord Christ saith, "If any man love me, he will keep my words; and we will make our abode with him."
author: Martin Luther
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: A consistent Christian may not have rapture; he has that which is much better than rapture—calmness—God's serene and perpetual presence.
author: F. W. Robertson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: I believe that into the weakest, saddest heart that opens to receive this Divine Guest, the Father and the Son will come and abide; and the exalted joy that abiding brings, what words can express! The Divine dwelling in the human, the Infinite in the finite, how marvelous! how glorious! This must be the real foretaste of heavenly joy the truest heaven we can know on earth.
author: A. H. K
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Nothing with God can be accidental.
author: Longfellow
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: History is the revelation of providence.
author: Kossuth
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The Providence that watches over the affairs of men works out of their mistakes, at times, a healthier issue than could have been accomplished by their wisest forethought.
author: J. A. Froude
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
There's a divinity that shapes our ends 
Rough-hew them how we will.
author: Shakspeare
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: God tempers the wind to the shorn lamb.
author: Laurence Sterne
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The moment we recognize God as supreme in power and infinitely good and loving toward all His intelligent creatures, that moment we admit the doctrine of universal and special providence.
author: J. G. Holland
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Whoever studies Divine providence, whether it be in relation to the events that concern us, our families, the cities and nations to which we belong; whoever studies the rise and fall of nations and empires, whoever looks at the clashing of armies, will perceive that these are only parts of one grand movement. God is marching on to the accomplishment of an appointed end; namely, the subjugation of the world to Himself.
author: J. M. Reid
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
God! Thy arm was here. 
And not to us, but to Thy arm alone, 
 Ascribe we all.
author: Shakspeare
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
God moves in a mysterious way 
 His wonders to perform; 
He plants His footsteps in the sea, 
 And rides upon the storm.
author: Cowper
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: I believe not only in "special providences," but in the whole universe as one infinite complexity of "special providences."
author: Charles Kingsley
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
My bark is wafted to the strand 
 By breath Divine; 
And on the helm there rests a hand 
 Other than mine.
author: Dean Alford
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
O, lonely tomb in Moab's land, 
 O, dark Bethpeor's hill, 
Speak to these curious hearts of ours, 
 And teach them to be still! 
God hath His mysteries of grace— 
 Ways that we cannot tell; 
He hides them deep, like the secret sleep, 
 Of him He loved so well.
author: Mrs. C. F. Alexander
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Let us always remember that God has never promised to supply our wishes, but only our wants, and these only as they arise from day to day.
author: Alexander Dickson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The sentences in the book of providence are sometimes long, and you must read a great way before you understand their meaning.
author: Matthew Henry
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Sometimes providences, like Hebrew letters, must be read backwards.
author: John Flavel
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: God works in a mysterious way in grace as well as in nature, concealing His operations under an imperceptible succession of events, and thus keeps us always in the darkness of faith.
author: Fenelon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: In all God's providences, it is good to compare His word and His works together; for we shall find a beautiful harmony between them, and that they mutually illustrate each other.
author: Matthew Henry
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Be an observer of providence; for God is showing you ever, by the way in which He leads you, whither He means to lead. Study your trials, your talents, the world's wants, and stand ready to serve God now, in whatever He brings to your hand.
author: Horace Bushnell
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We are never less alone than when we are in the society of a single, faithful friend; never less deserted than when we are carried in the arms of the All-Powerful.
author: Fenelon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: All spiritual strength for ourselves, all noble ties to one another, have their real source in that inner sanctuary where God denies His lonely audience to none. Its secrets are holy; its asylum, inviolate; its consolations, sure; and all are open to the simple heart-word, "Thou art my hiding-place."
author: James Martineau
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It was a touching answer of a Christian sailor, when asked why he remained so calm in a fearful storm, when the sea seemed ready to devour the ship. He was not sure that he could swim. "But," he said, "though I sink I shall only drop into the hollow of my Father's hand; for He holds all these waters there."
author: William Arnot
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There is many a thing which the world calls disappointment: but there is no such thing in the dictionary of faith. What to others are disappointments are to believers intimations of the will of God.
author: John Newton
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
God's ways seem dark, but, soon or late, 
 They touch the shining hills of day; 
The evil cannot brook delay, 
 The good can well afford to wait.
author: John G. Whittier
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Not a sorrow, not a burden, not a temptation, not a bereavement, not a disappointment, not a care, not a groan or tear, but has its antidote in God's rich and inexhaustible resources.
author: George C. Lorimer
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
As yonder tower outstretches to the earth 
The dark triangle of its shade alone 
When the clear day is shining on its top; 
So, darkness in the pathway of man's life 
Is but the shadow of God's providence, 
By the great Sun of wisdom cast thereon; 
And what is dark below is light in heaven.
author: J. G. Whittier
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
He sendeth sun, He sendeth shower,— 
Alike they're needful to the flower; 
And joys and tears alike are sent 
To give the soul fit nourishment. 
As comes to me or cloud or sun, 
Father! Thy will, not mine, be done.
author: S. F. Adams
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: God never makes us sensible of our weakness except to give us of His strength.
author: Fenelon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Even when the shadows of trial are falling around us, let us "pass through the cloud" with the sustaining motive—"All my wish, O God, is to please and glorify Thee!"
author: J. R. Macduff
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: God governs in the affairs of men; and if a sparrow cannot fall to the ground without His notice, neither can a kingdom rise without His aid.
author: Benjamin Franklin
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Thou art! directing, guiding all, Thou art! 
Direct my understanding then to Thee; 
Control my spirit, guide my wandering heart: 
Though but an atom midst immensity.
author: Derzhavin
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Can we outrun the heavens?
author: Shakspeare
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: God's will is the very perfection of all reason.
author: Edward Payson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Converting grace puts God on the throne, and the world at His footstool; Christ in the heart, and the world under His feet.
author: Joseph Alleine
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: However wickedness outstrips men, it has no wings to fly from God.
author: Shakspeare
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Was it possible that Napoleon should win the battle of Waterloo? We answer, No! Why? Because of Wellington? Because of Blucher? No! Because of God! For Bonaparte to conquer at Waterloo was not the law of the nineteenth century. It was time that this vast man should fall. He had been impeached before the Infinite! He had vexed God! Waterloo was not a battle. It was the change of front of the Universe!
author: Victor Hugo
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It is a great truth, "God reigns," and therefore grace reigns through righteousness unto eternal life, by Jesus Christ our Lord; and, therefore, no sinner on earth need ever despair.
author: Ichabod Spencer
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The moral government of God is a movement in a line onwards towards some grand consummation, in which the principles, indeed, are ever the same, but the developments are always new,—in which, therefore, no experience of the past can indicate with certainty what new openings of truth, what new manifestations of goodness, what new phases of the moral heaven may appear.
author: Mark Hopkins
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The hand of God never tires, nor are its movements aimless. It makes all things subservient to its designs, and, at every turn, disappoints the calculations of man, causing the most insignificant events to expand to the mightiest consequences, while those that have the appearance of mountains vanish into nothing.
author: John Lanahan
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Have faith! where'er thy bark is driven,— 
 The calm's disport, the tempest's mirth,— 
Know this! God rules the host of heaven, 
 The inhabitants of earth.
author: Schiller
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We worship unity in trinity, and trinity in unity; neither confounding the person nor dividing the substance. There is one person of the Father, another of the Son, and another of the Holy Ghost; but the Godhead of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost, is all one; the glory equal, the majesty co-eternal.
author: Tertullian
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Tell me how it is that in this room there are three candles and but one light, and I will explain to you the mode of the Divine existence.
author: John Wesley
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Snow is water, and ice is water, and water is water; these three are one.
author: Joseph Dare
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: God hides nothing. His very work from the beginning is revelation ,—a casting aside of veil after veil, a showing unto men of truth after truth. On and on from fact Divine He advances, until at length in His Son Jesus He unveils His very face.
author: George MacDonald
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Time that weakens all things else has but strengthened the impregnable position of the believer's faith and hope and confidence. And as, year by year, the tree adds another ring to its circumference, every age has added the testimony of its events to this great truth. "The grass withereth, and the flower fadeth, but the word of the Lord shall endure forever."
author: Thomas Guthrie
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: God's truth is too sacred to be expounded to superficial worldliness in its transient fit of earnestness.
author: F. W. Robertson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Goodness consists not in the outward things we do, but in the inward thing we are. To be is the great thing.
author: E. H. Chapin
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: How many people would like to be good, if only they might be good without taking trouble about it! They do not like goodness well enough to hunger and thirst after it, or to sell all that they have that they may buy it; they will not batter at the gate of the kingdom of heaven; but they look with pleasure on this or that aerial castle of righteousness, and think it would be rather nice to live in it.
author: George MacDonald
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Great hearts alone understand how much glory there is in being good.
author: Michelet
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

author: Charles Kingsley
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Be not simply good; be good for something.
author: Thoreau
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: No good thing is ever lost. Nothing dies, not even life which gives up one form only to resume another. No good action, no good example dies. It lives forever in our race. While the frame moulders and disappears, the deed leaves an indelible stamp, and moulds the very thought and will of future generations.
author: Samuel Smiles
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
For ever and ever, my darling, yes— 
 Goodness and love are undying; 
Only the troubles and cares of earth 
 Are winged from the first for flying. 
 Our way we plough 
 In the furrow "now;" 
 But after the tilling and growing the sheaf; 
 Soil for the root, but the sun for the leaf— 
 And God keepeth watch forever.
author: Mary Mapes Dodge
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Nothing that man ever invents will absolve him from the universal necessity of being good as God is good, righteous as God is righteous, and holy as God is holy.
author: Charles Kingsley
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: He who believes in goodness has the essence of all faith. He is a man "of cheerful yesterdays and confident to-morrows."
author: J. F. Clarke
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We cannot rekindle the morning beams of childhood; we cannot recall the noontide glory of youth; we cannot bring back the perfect day of maturity; we cannot fix the evening rays of age in the shadowy horizon; but we can cherish that goodness which is the sweetness of childhood, the joy of youth, the strength of maturity, the honor of old age, and the bliss of saints.
author: Henry Giles
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The gospel is the fulfillment of all hopes, the perfection of all philosophy, the interpretation of all revelation, the key to all the seeming contradictions of the physical and moral world.
author: Max Müller
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It is the grand endeavor of the gospel to communicate God to men.
author: Horace Bushnell
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: O, marvelous power of the Divine seed, which overpowers the strong man armed, softens obdurate hearts, and changes into divine men those who were brutalized in sin, and removed to an infinite distance from God.
author: John Wyckliffe
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: No one who has not examined patiently and honestly the other religions of the world can know what Christianity really is, or can join with such truth and sincerity in the words of St. Paul, "I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ."
author: Max Müller
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The main object of the gospel is to establish two principles, the corruption of nature, and the redemption by Jesus Christ.
author: Pascal
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Take Christ out of the gospel, and you take its very heart out. He has not only originated a system, but He has put Himself into it, as its very life and soul and power.
author: Herrick Johnson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The gospel breathes the spirit of love. Love is the fulfilling of its precepts, the pledge of its joys, and the evidence of its power.
author: Gardiner Spring
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Lincoln did but pour the soul of the nation into the monumental act of universal liberty; and that soul was inspired by the gospel.
author: Edward Thomson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The sweetness of the gospel lies mostly in pronouns, as me , my , thy . "Who loved me , and gave Himself for me ." "Christ Jesus my Lord." "Son, be of good cheer, thy sins are forgiven thee."
author: Martin Luther
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Just as in the Father's house there are many mansions, so to suit the various moods and divers cases of anxious souls, there are many chambers and compartments in the gospel citadel; but the very lowest and simplest, if you can only reach it, is Salvation. The nearest to the level, but still cleft in the Rock, is called "The Faithful Saying;" and above its doorway you read, "Jesus Christ came into the world to save sinners."
author: James Hamilton
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The idea of preaching the gospel to all nations alike, regardless of nationality, of internal divisions as to rank and color, complexion and religion, constituted the beginning of a new era in history. You cannot preach the gospel in its purity over the world, without proclaiming the doctrine of civil and religious liberty,—without overthrowing the barriers reared between nations and clans and classes of men,—without ultimately undermining the thrones of despots, and breaking off the shackles of slavery,—without making men everywhere free.
author: Albert Barnes
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: I thank God that the gospel is to be preached to every creature. There is no man so far gone, but the grace of God can reach him; no man so desperate or black, but He can forgive him.
author: D. L. Moody
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Assertion of truths known and felt, promulgation of truth from the high platform of truth itself, declaration of faith by the mouth of moral conviction—this is the New Testament method, and the true one.
author: J. G. Holland
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We can set our deeds to the music of a grateful heart, and seek to round our lives into a hymn—the melody of which will be recognized by all who come in contact with us, and the power of which shall not be evanescent, like the voice of the singer, but perenninal , like the music of the spheres.
author: Wm. M. Taylor
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Thankfulness is the tune of angels.
author: Edmund Spenser
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Did you ever think of the reason why the Psalms of David have come, like winged angels, down across all the realms and ages,—why they make the key-note of grateful piety in every Christian's soul, wherever he lives? Why? Because they are so full of gratitude. "Oh, that men would praise the Lord for His goodness and for His wonderful works to the children of men!"
author: A. A. Willets
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Do not let the empty cup be your first teacher of the blessings you had when it was full. Do not let a hard place here and there in the bed destroy your rest. Seek, as a plain duty, to cultivate a buoyant, joyous sense of the crowded kindnesses of God in your daily life.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The grave is a very small hillock, but we can see farther from it, when standing on it, than from the highest mountain in all the world.
author: A. Tholuck
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Dark lattice! letting in eternal day!
author: Young
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: For ages the world has been waiting and watching; millions, with broken hearts, have hovered around the yawning abyss; but no echo has come back from the engulfing gloom—silence, oblivion, covers all. If indeed they survive; if they went away whole and victorious, they give us no signals. We wait for years, but no messages come from the far-away shore to which they have gone.
author: Bishop R. S. Foster
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The earth doth not cover our beloved, but heaven hath received him; let us tarry for a while, and we shall be in his company.
author: St. Basil
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It is sweet to hold converse with the pious dead. A holy influence emanates from their blissful home, and fills the soul with a feeling of sacred and solemn awe. The spirit whispers peace, and fills the waiting caverns of the soul with the bright hope of again meeting those whom we believe to be in the abode of redeemed and happy spirits.
author: Mrs. Julia Norton
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There is a voice from the tomb sweeter than song. There is a remembrance of the dead to which we turn even from the charms of the living. O, the grave! the grave! It buries every error, covers every defect, extinguishes every resentment. From its peaceful bosom spring none but fond regrets and tender recollections.
author: Washington Irving
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The grave has a door on its inner side.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The greatest man is he who chooses the right with the most invincible resolution; who resists the sorest temptation from within and without; who bears the heavest burdens cheerfully; who is calmest in storms, and most fearless under menaces and frowns; whose reliance on truth, on virtue, and on God is most unfaltering.
author: Seneca
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Greatness lies not in being strong, but in the using of strength.
author: H. W. Beecher
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: True greatness does not consist so much in doing extraordinary things, as in conducting ordinary affairs with a noble demeanor and from a right motive. It is necessary and most profitable to remember the advice to Titus, "Showing all good fidelity in all things."
author: E. L. Magoon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: A solemn and religious regard to spiritual and eternal things is an indispensable element of all true greatness.
author: Daniel Webster
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: He who does the most good is the greatest man. Power, authority, dignity; honors, wealth, and station,—these are so far valuable as they put it into the hands of men to be more exemplary and more useful than they could be in an obscure and private life. But then these are means conducting to an end, and that end is goodness.
author: Bishop Jortin
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: A great man, I take it, is a man so inspired and permeated with the ideas of God and the Christly spirit as to be too magnanimous for vengeance, and too unselfish to seek his own ends.
author: David Thomas
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: He is truly great that is great in charity. He is truly great that is little in himself, and maketh no account of any height of honor. And he is truly learned that doeth the will of God, and forsaketh his own will.
author: Thomas à Kempis
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It is, in a great measure, by raising up and endowing great minds that God secures the advance of human affairs, and the accomplishment of His own plans on earth.
author: Albert Barnes
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There is but one method, and that is hard labor.
author: Sydney Smith
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The highest point of Christian experience is to press forward. It is a distinguishing trait in the character of every good man that he grows in grace. Grace in the heart as certainly improves and advances, as a tree thrives in a kindly and well watered soil.
author: Gardiner Spring
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It is not my strength that grows, so much as God's strength in me, which is given more abundantly as the days roll. It is so given on one condition. If my faith has laid hold of the infinite, the exhaustless, the immortal energy of God, unless there is something fearfully wrong about me, I shall be getting purer, nobler, wiser, more observant of His will; gentler, like Christ; every way fitter for His service, and for larger service, as the days increase.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Grow as a palm-tree on God's Mount Zion; howbeit shaken with winds, yet the root is fast.
author: Rutherford
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The vendors of flowers in the streets of London are wont to commend them to customers by crying: "All a blowing and a growing." It would be no small praise to Christians if we could say as much for them.
author: C. H. Spurgeon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: In proportion as we "grow in grace and in the knowledge of Christ," we shall grow in the desire that the Redeemer's sovereignty may be more widely and visibly extended.
author: Henry Melvill
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There is no such way to attain to greater measures of grace, as for a man to live up to that little grace he has.
author: Thomas Brooks
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It is the very nature of grace to make a man strive to be most eminent in that particular grace which is most opposed to his bosom sin.
author: Thomas Brooks
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: If you have nothing of the spirit of prayer, nothing of the love of the brotherhood, nothing of mortifying the spirit of the world, nothing of growth in grace, of cordial, habitual, persevering obedience to the Divine commands, how can it be that you have been brought nigh by the blood of Christ?
author: Gardiner Spring
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: May we grow more and more like God and heaven, more gracious, helpful, and sweet-minded; and when at last Thou hast served Thyself by us, may we fall asleep in Jesus, and find it no sleep, but everlasting waking in Jesus.
author: H. W. Beecher
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: A large part of Christian virtue consists in right habits.
author: Paley
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Give a child the habit of sacredly regarding the truth—of carefully respecting the property of others—of scrupulously abstaining from all acts of improvidence which can involve him in distress, and he will just as likely think of rushing into the element in which he cannot breathe, as of lying or cheating or stealing.
author: Lord Brougham
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Centres, or centre-pieces of wood, are put by builders under an arch of stone while it is in the process of construction till the key-stone is put in. Just such is the use Satan makes of pleasures to construct evil habits upon; the pleasure lasts till the habit is fully formed; but that done, the habit may stand eternal. The pleasures are sent for firewood, and the hell begins in this life.
author: Coleridge
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Infinite toil would not enable you to sweep away a mist, but by ascending a little you may often look over it altogether. So it is with our moral improvement; we wrestle fiercely with a vicious habit, which could have no hold upon us if we ascended to a higher atmosphere.
author: Sir Arthur Helps
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Habit if not resisted soon becomes necessity.
author: St. Augustine
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Every sinful act is another cord woven into that mighty cable of habit, which binds the spirit to the throne of darkness.
author: David Thomas
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The diminutive chains of habit are seldom heavy enough to be felt, till they are too strong to be broken.
author: Samuel Johnson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Brethren, happiness is not our being's end and aim. The Christian's aim is perfection, not happiness; and every one of the sons of God must have something of that spirit which marked his Master.
author: F. W. Robertson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There is something better for us in the world than happiness. We will take happiness as the incident of this, gladly and gratefully. We will add a thousand fold to the happiness of the present in the fearlessness of the future which it brings; but we will not place happiness first, and thus cloud our heads with doubts, and fill our hearts with discontent. In the blackest soils grow the richest flowers, and the loftiest and strongest trees spring heavenward among the rocks.
author: J. G. Holland
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: In vain do they talk of happiness who never subdued an impulse in obedience to a principle. He who never sacrificed a present to a future good, or a personal to a general one, can speak of happiness only as the blind do of colors.
author: Horace Mann
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The sacrifices required in the Christian life are necessary to emancipate the soul, and raise it above its servile dependence on condition. They are losses of mere happiness, and for just that reason they are preparations of joy.
author: Horace Bushnell
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It is a great truth, wonderful as it is undeniable, that all our happiness—temporal, spiritual, and eternal—consists in one thing; namely, in resigning ourselves to God, and in leaving ourselves with Him, to do with us and in us just as He pleases.
author: Madame Guyon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Happiness is neither within us nor without us, it is the union of ourselves with God.
author: Pascal
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Happiness is not the end of duty, it is a constituent of it. It is in it and of it; not an equivalent, but an element.
author: Henry Giles
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: When we are not too anxious about happiness and unhappiness, but devote ourselves to the strict and unsparing performance of duty, then happiness comes of itself—nay, even springs from the midst of a life of troubles and anxieties and privations.
author: Humboldt
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: So long as you do not quarrel with sin, you will never be a truly happy man.
author: J. C. Ryle
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Beware what earth calls happiness; beware 
All joys, but joys that never can expire.
author: Young
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: All that I have known of happiness has come to me through being made a child again. The efforts to find something to satisfy my inward longings, which were made through the intellectual nature, were as powerless to sustain me as a theory of bread-making would be to satisfy a hungry man. How far our sorrows and losses may help us in making us willing to receive what Heaven bestows, I know not; but when we find how fruitless our efforts are, we are as helpless as little children. Then, if humble and willing to wait, Jesus Christ will Himself come to us, a dear, human friend; and then we shall be surprised to find He was walking with us all the while when the path seemed so dark and lonely, and, dear me! how different every thing now appears. The world looks too beautiful to leave, yet, somehow, we were never so willing to leave it.
author: The New York Observer
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The soul's calm sunshine.
author: Pope
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Happiness is not perfected until it is shared.
author: Jane Porter
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: I will tell you what to hate. Hate hypocrisy, hate cant, hate indolence, oppression, injustice; hate Pharisaism; hate them as Christ hated them—with a deep, living, godlike hatred.
author: F. W. Robertson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We ourselves also were sometimes living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.
author: Bible
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Thank Him for health. Consecrate it as His trust to innocent enjoyment, manly effort, social usefulness, and preparation for an honorable and holy career.
author: W. E. Channing
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Christ's gospel could never have been delivered by one who was diseased.
author: J. McC. Holmes
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
O rest of rests! O peace serene, eternal! 
 Thou ever livest, and Thou changest never! 
And in the secret of Thy presence dwelleth 
 Fullness of joy, forever and forever.
author: Mrs. H. B. Stowe
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We are born for a higher destiny than earth; there is a realm where the rainbow never fades, where the stars will be spread before us like islands that slumber on the ocean, and where the beings that pass before us like shadows will stay in our presence forever.
author: Bulwer Lytton
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
When this passing world is done, 
 When has sunk yon, glowing sun, 
When we stand with Christ in glory, 
 Looking o'er life's finished story, 
Then, Lord, shall I fully know— 
 Not till then how much I owe.
author: Robert McCheyne
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: I cannot be content with less than heaven.
author: P. J. Bailey
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Heaven is attracting to itself whatever is congenial to its nature, is enriching itself by the spoils of earth, and collecting within its capacious bosom whatever is pure, permanent, and divine.
author: Robert Hall
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: No wearisome days, no sorrowful nights; no hunger or thirst; no anxiety or fears; no envies, no jealousies, no breaches of friendship, no sad separations, no distrusts or forebodings, no self-reproaches, no enmities, no bitter regrets, no tears, no heartaches; "And there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain; for the former things are passed away."
author: Bishop R. S. Foster
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
No more fatigue, no more distress, 
Nor sin nor death shall reach the place; 
No groans shall mingle with the songs 
That warble from immortal tongues.
author: Philip Doddridge
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Christ and His cross are not separable in this life, howbeit Christ and His cross part at heaven's door, for there is no house-room for crosses in heaven. One tear, one sigh, one sad heart, one fear, one loss, one thought of trouble cannot find lodging there.
author: Rutherford
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
"A little while," and the load 
 Shall drop at the pilgrim's feet, 
Where the steep and thorny road 
 Doth merge in the golden street.
author: W. Gladden
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: After the fever of life—after wearinesses, sicknesses, fightings and despondings, languor and fretfulness, struggling and failing, struggling and succeeding—after all the changes and chances of this troubled and unhealthy state, at length comes death—at length the white throne of God—at length the beatific vision.
author: Newman
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: And then, the quiet of the green, inland valleys of our Father's land, where no tempest comes any more, nor the loud winds are ever heard, nor the salt sea is ever seen; but perpetual calm and blessedness; all mystery gone, and all rebellion hushed and silenced, and all unrest at an end forever! "No more sea;" but, instead of that wild and yeasty chaos of turbulent waters, there shall be the river that makes glad the city of God, the river of water of life, that proceeds "out of the throne of God and of the Lamb."
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: An everlasting tranquillity is, in my imagination, the highest possible felicity, because I know of no felicity on earth higher than that which a peaceful mind and contented heart afford.
author: Zimmerman
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Selfishness, eager for a heaven of enjoyment, is quite a different thing in the soul from love and purity and truth, yearning together for what is their natural element.
author: Wm. Mountford
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The redeemed shall walk there.
author: Bible
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: What tranquillity will there be in heaven! Who can express the fullness and blessedness of this peace! What a calm is this! How sweet and holy and joyous! What a haven of rest to enter, after having passed through the storms and tempests of this world, in which pride and selfishness and envy and malice and scorn and contempt and contention and vice are as waves of a restless ocean, always rolling, and often dashed about in violence and fury! What a Canaan of rest to come to, after going through this waste and howling wilderness, full of snares and pitfalls and poisonous serpents, where no rest could be found.
author: Jonathan Edwards
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: O, land of rest, how near thou art! O, judgment-seat of Jesus, how thin are the clouds that veil thee! Through the rifts of cloudland shine rays from this righteous crown. It is "laid up" for him whose hope can never be satisfied with less than the presence of the King.
author: Stephen H. Tyng, Jr
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: One should go to sleep as homesick passengers do, saying "Perhaps in the morning we shall see the shore."
author: H. W. Beecher
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: And looking back upon "the sea that brought us thither," we shall behold its waters flashing in the light of that everlasting morning, and hear them breaking into music upon the eternal shore. And then, brethren, when all the weary night- watchers on the stormy ocean of life are gathered together around Him who watched with them from His throne on the bordering mountains of eternity, where the day shines forever—then He will seat them at His table in His kingdom, and none will need to ask, "Who art Thou?" or, "Where am I?" "for all shall know it is the Lord," and the full, perfect, unchangeable vision of His blessed face will be heaven.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: In our Father's house it will not be the pearl gate or the streets of gold that will make us happy. But oh, how transcendently glad shall we be when we see our Lord. Perhaps in that "upper room," also, He may show us His hands and His side, and we may cry out with happy Thomas, "My Lord and my God!"
author: T. L. Cuyler
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Oh, heaven without my Saviour 
 Would be no heaven to me; 
Dim were the walls of jasper— 
 Rayless the crystal sea. 
He gilds earth's darkest valleys 
 With light and joy and peace; 
What then must be the radiance 
 When night and death shall cease?
author: Helen L. Parmlee
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.
author: Bible
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Perhaps heaven may not be so far away as we fancy; and if our eyes were not holden, we should see angels ascending and descending, and blessed spirits thronging all about us.
author: A. H. K
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There is not such a great difference between grace and glory after all. Grace is the bud, and glory is the blossom. Grace is glory begun; and glory is grace perfected. It won't come hard to people that are serving God down here to do it when they go up yonder. They will change places, but they won't change employments.
author: D. L. Moody
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: I change my place, but not my company. While here I have sometimes walked with God, and now I go to rest with Him.
author: Dr. Preston
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Every Christian that goes before us from this world is a ransomed spirit waiting to welcome us in heaven.
author: Jonathan Edwards
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: What we sow here, we reap there! Can it be supposed that the soul will enjoy a reward or endure a retribution for deeds of which it has no recollection? Is the thing possible? Will it enjoy the bliss of heaven, praising Christ forever as its great Saviour, without any remembrance of the sins and sufferings from which He redeemed and saved it? The idea is absurd.
author: Bishop R. S. Foster
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Death must obliterate all memories and affections and ideas and laws, or the awakening in the next world will be amid the welcomes, and loves and raptures of those who left us with tearful farewells, and with dying promises that they would wait to .mw-parser-output .wst-tooltip{cursor:help;border-bottom:thin dotted cornflowerblue}.mw-parser-output .wst-tooltip-nodash{border-bottom:none} welcomes us when we should arrive. And so they do. Not sorrowfully, not anxiously, but lovingly, they wait to bid us welcome.
author: Bishop R. S. Foster
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: With Christ, and like Christ, and not love our friends! Impossible! when He loves them so tenderly. Going into the fuller presence of Him whose very name is "Love" can never make our hearts less loving.
author: A. H. K
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
I shall know the loved who have gone before, 
 And joyfully sweet will the meeting be, 
When over the river, the peaceful river, 
 The angel of death shall carry me.
author: N. A. W. Priest
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Then re-united to the friends with whom we took sweet counsel upon earth, we shall recount our toil, only to heighten our ecstasy; and call to mind the toil and the din of war, only that, with a more bounding throb and a richer song, we may feel and celebrate the wonders of redemption.
author: Henry Melvill
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Blessed loves! how happy they have made us on the earth; what will they be when they have deepened through ages, with no alloy of envy or suspicion or selfishness or sorrow?
author: Bishop R. S. Foster
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: What delight will it afford to renew the sweet counsel we have taken together, to recount the toils, the combats, and the labor of the way, and to approach, not the house, but the throne of God, in company, in order to join in the symphonies of heavenly voices, and lose ourselves amidst the splendors and fruitions of the beatific vision.
author: Robert Hall
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: God would never have let us long for our friends with such a strong and holy love, if they were not waiting for us.
author: Wm. Mountford
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: They are kings and priests unto God. They wear crowns that flash in the everlasting light. They wear robes that are spotlessly white. They wave victorious palms. They sing anthems of such exceeding sweetness as no earthly choirs ever approach. They stand before the throne. They fly on ministries of love. They muse on the top of Mount Zion. They meditate on the banks of the river of life. They are rapturous with ecstasies of love. God wipes away all tears from their eyes.
author: Bishop R. S. Foster
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: In heaven, knowledge shall be commensurate with the enlarged powers of the glorified soul.
author: T. L. Cuyler
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The joys of heaven are not the joys of passive contemplation, of dreamy remembrance, of perfect repose; but they are described thus: "They rest not day nor night." "His servants serve Him, and see His face."
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Man has in his power, now developed, nothing more than a mere hint or initial sign of what is to be the real stature of his personality in the process of his everlasting development. We exist here only in the small, that God may have us in a state of flexibility, and bend or fashion us, at the best advantage, to the model of His own great life and character.
author: Horace Bushnell
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It doth not yet appear what we shall be. We lie here in our nest, unfledged and weak, guessing dimly at our future, and scarce believing what even now appears. But the power is in us, and that power is finally to be revealed. And what a revelation will that be!
author: Horace Bushnell
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Will not this be the description of our future being—"reaching forth unto those things which are before?" I believe that we shall thus live through all the eternities that are before us, growing wiser, nobler, stronger, greater; plunging deeper into God, and being more and more filled with more and more of Him. So we shall move forever as in ascending spirals that rise ever higher, and draw ever closer to the throne we compass and to Him that dwells alone; ever perfect, yet ever growing, for we have an inexhaustible Saviour to absorb into our hearts, and we have hearts that never reach the ultimate bound and term of their indefinite possibility of receiving.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Heaven is endless longing, accompanied with an endless fruition—a longing which is blessedness, a longing which is life.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: As we look up into these glorious culminations, how grand life becomes! To be forever with the Lord, and forever changing into His likeness, and, still more, forever deepening in the companionship of His thought and bliss, "from glory to glory,"—could we desire more?
author: Bishop R. S. Foster
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We should carry up our affections to the mansions prepared for us above, where eternity is the measure, felicity the state, angels the company, the Lamb the light, and God the inheritance and portion of His people forever.
author: Jeremy Taylor
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Yes, it is a truth that for a good man,—honored, beloved, useful,—with all around him that God ever gives to His children here;—nay, with all that God could give him of earth, it would be "gain" to die. Heaven is a better, a happier, a more desirable world than this is or can be.
author: Albert Barnes
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Beyond the smiling and the weeping, 
 I shall be soon; 
 Beyond the waking and the sleeping, 
 Beyond the sowing and the reaping, 
 I shall be soon! 
 Love, rest, and home— 
Sweet hope! Lord, tarry not, but come!
author: Horatius Bonar
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Oh, when shall the night be gone, the shadows flee away, and the morning of that long, long day, without cloud or night, dawn?
author: Rutherford
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Rejoice, oh! grieving heart, 
 The hours fly past; 
With each some sorrow dies, 
With each some shadow flies, 
 Until at last 
The red dawn in the east 
Bids weary night depart, 
 And pain is past.
author: A. A. Procter
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
When the day of toil is done, 
When the race of life is run, 
Father, grant Thy wearied one 
 Rest for evermore! 
When the heart by sorrow tried 
Feels at length its throbs subside, 
Bring us, where all tears are dried, 
 Joy for evermore!
author: C. C. Scholefield
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Millions of spiritual beings walk the earth unseen, 
Both when we wake, and when we sleep.
author: Milton
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Hands of invisible spirits touch the strings 
Of that mysterious instrument, the soul, 
And play the prelude of our fate.
author: Longfellow
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Do we not hear voices, gentle and great, and some of them like the voices of departed friends,—do we not hear them saying to us, "Come up hither?"
author: Wm. Mountford
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Yes, thank God! there is rest—many an interval of saddest, sweetest rest—even here, when it seems as if evening breezes from that other land, laden with fragrance, played upon the cheeks, and lulled the heart. There are times, even on the stormy sea, when a gentle whisper breathes softly as of heaven, and sends into the soul a dream of ecstasy which can never again wholly die, even amidst the jar and whirl of daily life. How such whispers make the blood stop and the flesh creep with a sense of mysterious communion! How singularly such moments are the epochs of life—the few points that stand out prominently in the recollection after the flood of years has buried all the rest, as all the low shore disappears, leaving only a few rock points visible at high tide.
author: F. W. Robertson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There are times in the history of men and nations, when they stand so near the vail that separates mortals from the immortals, time from eternity, and men from their God, that they can almost hear the beatings, and feel the pulsations, of the heart of the Infinite.
author: James A. Garfield
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It may be that at this moment every battlement of heaven is alive with the redeemed. There is a sainted mother watching for her daughter. Have you no response to that long hushed voice which has prayed for you so often? And for you, young man, are there no voices there that have prayed for you? And are there none whom you promised once to meet again, if not on earth, in heaven?
author: D. L. Moody
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: What will you do in a world where the Holy Spirit never strives; where every soul is fully left to its own depravity; and where there is no leisure for repentance, if there were even the desire, but where there is too much present pain to admit repentance; where they gnaw their tongues with pain, and blaspheme the God of heaven?
author: James Hamilton
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: An immortality of pain and tears; an infinity of wretchedness and despair; the blackness of darkness across which conscience will forever shoot her clear and ghastly flashes,—like lightning streaming over a desert when midnight and tempest are there; weeping and wailing and gnashing of teeth; long, long eternity, and things that will make eternity seem longer,—making each moment seem eternity,—oh, miserable condition of the damned!
author: Richard Fuller
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The Lamb is, indeed, the emblem of love; but what so terrible as the wrath of the Lamb? The depth of the mercy despised is the measure of the punishment of him that despiseth. No more fearful words than those of the Saviour. The threatenings of the law were temporal , those of the gospel are eternal . It is Christ who reveals the never-dying worm, the unquenchable fire, and He who contrasts with the eternal joys of the redeemed the everlasting woes of the lost . His loving arms would enfold the whole human race, but not while impenitent or unbelieving; the benefits of His redemption are conditional.
author: Edward Thomson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Many might go to heaven with half the labor they go to hell, if they would venture their industry the right way.
author: Ben Jonson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The longer men sin, the more easily they can; for every act of transgression weakens conscience, stupefies intellect, hardens hearts, adds force to bad habits, and takes force from good example. And, surely, there is nothing in such associations, as wicked affinities will insure to the sinner in the future state, to incline him to repentance.
author: Edward Thomson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
The mind is its own place, and in itself 
Can make a heaven of hell, a hell of heaven.
author: Milton
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: True heroism is alike positive and progressive. It sees in right the duty which should dominate, and in truth the principle which should prevail. And hence it never falters in the faith that always and everywhere sin must be repressed, and righteousness exalted.
author: J. McC. Holmes
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Never was there a time, in the history of the world, when moral heroes were more needed. The world waits for such, the providence of God has commanded science to labor and prepare the way for such. For them she is laying her iron tracks, and stretching her wires, and bridging the oceans. But where are they? Who shall breathe into our civil and political relations the breath of a higher life? Who shall touch the eyes of a paganized science, and of a pantheistic philosophy, that they may see God? Who shall consecrate to the glory of God, the triumphs of science? Who shall bear the life-boat to the stranded and perishing nations?
author: Mark Hopkins
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The courage of Daniel is true heroism. It is not physical daring, such as beneath some proud impulse will rush upon an enemy's steel; it is not reckless valor, sporting with a life which ill-fortune has blighted or which despair has made intolerable; it is not the passiveness of the stoic, through whose indifferent heart no tides of feeling flow; it is the calm courage which reflects upon its alternatives, and deliberately chooses to do right; it is the determination of Christian principle, whose foot resteth on the rock, and whose eye pierceth into heaven.
author: Wm. M. Punshon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: With quaint manners and quaint names these men had the hero's heart and the confessor's faith. Their faith was, indeed, their strength. Strong in the supremacy of conscience, in that real earnestness which springs from conviction, and which prompts to enterprise; far-sighted in political sagacity, because seeing Him that is invisible; shrewd enough to know that the truest policy for the life that now is, is a reverent recognition of the life that is to come, they were brave in endurance and patient under trial; and never losing sight of the principle for which they struggled, and of the purpose of their voyage afar, they "won the wilderness for God."
author: Wm. M. Punshon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Don't aim at any impossible heroisms. Strive rather to be quiet in your own sphere. Don't live in the cloudland of some transcendental heaven; do your best to bring the glory of a real heaven down, and ray it out upon your fellows in this work-day world. Seek to make trade bright with a spotless integrity, and business lustrous with the beauty of holiness.
author: Wm. M. Punshon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The grandest of heroic deeds are those which are performed within four walls and in domestic privacy.
author: Jean Paul Richter
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The calm, tranquil energy of the Redeemer's soul; the deep strength of principle which nothing could shake; the serene courage which looked down upon menaces, clamor, contumely, sacrifice, death,—this is the temper which pours contempt upon the intrepidity of heroes, but which the Holy Spirit infuses into the humble Christian.
author: Richard Fuller
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Holiness is an unselfing of ourselves.
author: F. W. Faber
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Holiness is religious principle put into motion. It is the love of God sent forth into circulation, on the feet, and with the hands of love to men. It is faith gone to work. It is charity coined into actions, and devotion breathing benedictions on human suffering, while it goes up in intercession to the Father of all piety.
author: F. D. Huntington
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: And now because you are His child, live as a child of God; be redeemed from the life of evil, which is false to your nature, into the life of goodness, which is the truth of your being. Scorn all that is mean; hate all that is false; struggle with all that is impure. Live the simple, lofty life which befits an heir of immortality.
author: F. W. Robertson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The inquirer after holiness should associate with those whose intelligence will instruct him; whose example will guide him; whose conversation will inspire him; whose cautions will warn him.
author: John Angel James
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Holiness is happiness; and the more you have of the former, the more you will undoubtedly enjoy of the latter.
author: John Angel James
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: I make it my constant prayer that God would most graciously be pleased to dispose us all to do justice, to love mercy, and to demean ourselves with that charity, humility, and pacific temper of mind, which were the characteristics of the Divine Author of our blessed religion; without a humble imitation of whose example in these things, we can never hope to be a happy nation.
author: George Washington
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: How much better it is to see men live exactly than to hear them argue with subtlety!
author: John Flavel
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: A man's life is an appendix to his heart.
author: South
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Just as sure as the days go by, Jesus will come to us, looking for fruit; and He will come in personal hunger, needing and longing for the fruit which we might have ready for Him.
author: H. Clay Trumbull
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: God looketh upon any thing we say, or any thing we do, and if He seeth Christ in it, He accepteth it; but if there be no Christ, He putteth it away as a foul thing.
author: C. H. Spurgeon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Harbor no thought, neither do any act you would be unwilling the whole world should know.
author: Albert Matthews
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Seek and possess holiness, and consolation will follow, as assuredly as warmth follows the dispensation of the rays of the sun.
author: Upham
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: What Christianity in her antagonism with every form of unbelief most needs is holy living.
author: Christlieb
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The narrow way, the way of holiness, not only leads to life, but it is life . Walking there, serene are our days, peaceful our nights, happy—high above the disorders and miseries of a wretched world—shall be our hourly communion with God; happy—full of assurance, of calm and sacred triumph, shall be our dying hour.
author: Richard Fuller
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We must keep up the standard of Christian living in the Christian laborer. Clean hands are needed to do Christian work. Character is before co-operation, being before doing. "Take heed unto thyself, and unto the doctrine."
author: John Hall
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Holiness is the architectural plan upon which God buildeth up His living temple.
author: C. H. Spurgeon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Are angels my attendants? Then I should walk worthy of my companionship. Am I so soon to go and dwell with angels? Then I should be pure. Are these feet so soon to tread the courts of heaven? Is this tongue so soon to unite with heavenly beings in praising God? Are these eyes so soon to look on the throne of eternal glory, and on the ascended Redeemer? Then these feet and eyes and lips should be pure and holy; and I should be dead to the world, and live for heaven.
author: Albert Barnes
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: If it be heaven toward which we journey, it will be holiness in which we delight; for if we cannot now rejoice in having God for our portion, where is our meetness for a world in which God is to be all in all forever and forever?
author: Henry Melvill
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource
