Take it into your own hearts, and think about it,—a kingdom, a judgment-seat, a crown, a gathered universe; separation, decision, execution of the sentence.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We are all approaching that dread tribunal. However diversified our paths, they all converge toward that common centre. The young, with their elastic tread, are striding to the judgment; the old, with their tottering limbs are creeping to the judgment; the rich in their splendid equipages are driving to the judgment; the poor, in rags and barefooted, are walking to the judgment. The Christian making God's statutes his song, is a pilgrim to the judgment; the sinner, treading upon the mercy of Jesus, and trampling upon His blood, is hastening to the judgment. "We must all appear before the judgment-seat of Christ."
author: Richard Fuller
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Truly at the day of judgment we shall not be examined as to what we have read, but as to what we have done; not as to how well we have spoken, but as to how religiously we have lived.
author: Thomas à Kempis
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

author: John Keble
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Justice is a constant and perpetual will to render to every one that which is his own.
author: Justinian
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: At some time, here or hereafter, every account must be settled, and every debt paid in full.
author: J. H. Vincent
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We are accounted righteous before God, only for the merit of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ by faith, and not for our own works or deservings.
author: Articles of Methodist Episcopal Church
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Justification is an act of God's free grace, wherein He pardoneth all our sins, and accepteth us as righteous in His sight, only for the righteousness of Christ imputed to us, and received by faith alone.
author: Westminster Catechism
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Justification is the act of God as a Judge; adoption as a Father; by the former we are discharged from condemnation, and accepted as righteous; by the latter we are made the children of God and joint-heirs with Christ.
author: John Guyse
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Justification is the work of Christ for us; sanctification the work of the Spirit in us; justification is perfect at once; sanctification is progressive; justification is before sanctification, and sanctification is the fruit of justification; consequently the evidence of our justification is our sanctification.
author: John Angel James
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Justification by faith is the answer to that momentous question, "How shall man be just with God?" And the reply is, "Not by works of his own, but by faith in the work of another, that is Christ." He must have a righteousness in which to stand before a righteous and a holy, as well as a merciful God. He has no such righteousness of his own. Christ is the end of the law for righteousness unto him.
author: John Angel James
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The thief upon the cross and the beloved John were alike complete in Christ.
author: Anna Shipton
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: I expect to pass through this life but once. If therefore there be any kindnesses I can show, or any good thing I can do to any fellow beings, let me do it now. Let me not defer or neglect it, for I shall not pass this way again.
author: Mrs. A. B. Hegeman
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Life is made up, not of great sacrifices or duties, but of little things, in which smiles and kindnesses and small obligations, given habitually, are what win and preserve the heart, and secure comfort.
author: Sir Humphry Davy
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: If you consider that the constant tenor of the gospel precepts is to promote love, peace, and good-will amongst men, you will not doubt that the cultivation of an amiable disposition is a great part of your religious duty; since nothing leads more directly to the breach of charity, and to the injury and molestation of our fellow-creatures than the indulgence of an ill-temper.
author: Hester Chapone
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Kindness has converted more sinners than either zeal, eloquence, or learning.
author: F. W. Faber
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Every one of us knows how painful it is to be called by malicious names, to have his character undermined by false insinuations, to be overreached in a bargain, to be neglected by those who rise in life, to be thrust on one side by those who have stronger wills and stouter hearts. Every one knows, also, the pleasure of receiving a kind look, a warm greeting, a hand held out to help in distress, a difficulty solved, a higher hope revealed for this world or the next. By that pain and by that pleasure let us judge what we should do to others.
author: Dean Stanley
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: He had a face like a benediction.
author: Cervantes
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The end of learning is to know God, and out of that knowledge to love Him and imitate Him.
author: Milton
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Real knowledge, like every thing else of the highest value, is not to be obtained easily. It must be worked for,—studied for,—thought for,—and, more than all, it must be prayed for.
author: Thomas Arnold
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: To understand at all what life means, one must begin with Christian belief. And I think knowledge may be sorrow with a man unless he loves.
author: Wm. Mountford
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: As revelation is the great strengthener of reason, the march of mind which leaves the Bible in the rear, is an advance, like that of our first parents in Paradise, towards knowledge, but, at the same time, towards death.
author: Henry Melvill
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Knowledge is folly unless grace guide it.
author: George Herbert
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: An uneducated population may be degraded: a population educated, but not in righteousness, will be ungovernable. The one may be slaves, the other must be tyrants.
author: Henry Melvill
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Every increase of knowledge may possibly render depravity more depraved, as well as it may increase the strength of virtue. It is in itself only power; and its value depends on its application.
author: Sydney Smith
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Learning, without Christ, is among the most dangerous attainments the human race has ever secured and one of the most unsatisfying.
author: Bishop Haven
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: If thou knewest the whole Bible by heart, and the sayings of all the philosophers, what would it profit thee without the love of God and without grace?
author: Thomas à Kempis
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: What a man knows should find its expression in what he does. The value of superior knowledge is chiefly in that it leads to a performing manhood.
author: C. N. Bovee
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Let me always remember that it is not the amount of religious knowledge which I have, but the amount which I use, that determines my religious position and character.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The essential difference between that knowledge which is, and that which is not conclusive evidence of Christian character, lies in this: the object of the one is the agreement of the several parts of a theological proposition; the object of the other is moral beauty, the intrinsic loveliness of God and Divine things. The sinner sees and hates; the saint sees and loves.
author: Gardiner Spring
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There is oftentimes a great deal of knowledge where there is but little wisdom to improve that knowledge. It is not the most knowing Christian but the most wise Christian that sees, avoids, and escapes Satan's snares. Knowledge without wisdom is like mettle in a blind horse, which is often an occasion of the rider's fall.
author: Thomas Brooks
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
How empty learning, and how vain is art, 
But as it mends the life, and guides the heart!
author: Young
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The wish falls often warm upon my heart that I may learn nothing here that I cannot continue in the other world; that I may do nothing here but deeds that will bear fruit in heaven.
author: Jean Paul Richter
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Much learning shows how little mortals know; 
Much wealth, how little worldlings can enjoy.
author: Young
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: As all true virtue, wherever found, is a ray of the life of the All-Holy; so all solid knowledge, all really accurate thought, descends from the Eternal Reason, and ought, when we apprehend it, to guide us upwards to Him.
author: H. P. Liddon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Young converts are sometimes so taken up with religious feeling and doing as to forget the importance even, in reference to that of knowing . "Grow in grace and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ."
author: John Angel James
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Real knowledge never promoted either turbulence or unbelief; but its progress is the forerunner of liberality and enlightened toleration.
author: Lord Brougham
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Labor is not, as some have erroneously supposed, a penal clause of the original curse. There was labor, bright, healthful, unfatiguing, in unfallen Paradise. By sin, labor became drudgery—the earth was restrained from her spontaneous fertility, and the strong arm of the husbandman was required, not to develop, but to "subdue" it. But labor in itself is noble, and is necessary for the ripe unfolding of the highest life.
author: Wm. M. Punshon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Labor is the true alchemist that beats out in patient transmutation the baser metals into gold.
author: Wm. M. Punshon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Nothing is denied to well-directed labor; nothing is ever to be attained without it.
author: Sir Joshua Reynolds
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It is intended that we shall accomplish all, through law, that we can accomplish for ourselves. God gives every bird its food, but does not throw it into the nest. He does not unearth the good that the earth contains, but He puts it in our way, and gives us the means of getting it ourselves.
author: J. G. Holland
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Blessed is the man who has found his work; let him ask no other blessedness. Know thy work, and do it; and work at it like Hercules. One monster there is in the world, the idle man.
author: Thomas Carlyle
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: God does not give excellence to men but as the reward of labor.
author: Sir Joshua Reynolds
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: No man is born into the world whose work is not born with him. There is always work, and tools to work withal, for those who will.
author: H. W. Beecher
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Work is God's ordinance as truly as prayer.
author: George D. Boardman
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The virtues, like the body, become strong more by labor than by nourishment.
author: Jean Paul Richter
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The more we work the more we need to pray. In this day of activity there is great danger, not of doing too much, but of praying too little for so much work.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Jesus aimed to impregnate the natural with the spiritual, and to resolve all our avocations into a heavenly discipline.
author: Bishop Clark
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The gospel freely admitted makes a man happy. It gives him peace with God, and makes him happy in God. It gives to industry a noble, contented look which selfish drudgery never wore; and from the moment that a man begins to do his work for his Saviour's sake, he feels that the most ordinary employments are full of sweetness and dignity, and that the most difficult are not impossible. And if any of you, my friends, is weary with his work, if dissatisfaction with yourself or sorrow of any kind disheartens you, if at any time you feel the dull paralysis of conscious sin, or the depressing influence of vexing thoughts, look to Jesus, and be happy. Be happy, and your joyful work will prosper well.
author: Wilberforce
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Man must work. That is certain as the sun. But he may work grudgingly, or he may work gratefully; he may work as a man, or he may work as a machine. He cannot always choose his work, but he can do it in a generous temper, and with an up-looking heart. There is no work so rude, that he may not exalt it; there is no work so impassive, that he may not breathe a soul into it; there is no work so dull, that he may not enliven it.
author: Henry Giles
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: No man is base who does a true work; for true action is the highest being. No man is miserable that does a true work; for right action is the highest happiness. No man is isolated that does a true work; for useful action is the highest harmony—it is the highest harmony with nature and with souls—it is living association with men and it is practical fellowship with God.
author: Henry Giles
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Labor is sweet, for Thou hast toiled, 
 And care is light, for Thou hast cared; 
Let not our works with self be soiled, 
 Nor in unsimple ways ensnared. 
Through life's long day and death's dark night, 
 O gentle Jesus! be our light.
author: F. W. Faber
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: A man's labors must pass like the sunrises and sunsets of the world. The next thing, not the last, must be his care.
author: George MacDonald
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Not worthy, Lord, to gather up the crumbs 
 With trembling hand that from Thy table fall, 
A weary, heavy laden sinner comes 
 To plead Thy promise and obey Thy call.
author: E. H. Bickersteth
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We do not presume to come to this Thy table, O merciful Lord, trusting in our own righteousness, but in Thy manifold and great mercies. We are not worthy so much as to gather up the crumbs under Thy table. But Thou art the same Lord, whose property is always to have mercy. Grant us, therefore, gracious Lord, so to eat the flesh of Thy dear Son Jesus Christ, and to drink His blood, that our sinful souls and bodies may be made clean by His death, and washed through His most precious blood, and that we may evermore dwell in Him, and He in us.
author: Methodist Book of Discipline
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We do not come to the Lord's Supper to testify thereby that we are perfect and righteous in ourselves; but on the contrary considering that we seek our life out of ourselves in Jesus Christ, we acknowledge that we lie in the midst of death. Therefore, notwithstanding we feel many infirmities and miseries in ourselves; as namely, that we have not perfect faith, and that we do not give ourselves to serve God with that zeal as we are bound, but have daily to strive with the weakness of our faith, and the evil lusts of our flesh; yet since we are by the grace of the Holy Ghost sorry for these weaknesses, and earnestly desirous to fight against our unbelief, and to live according to all the commandments of God; therefore we rest assured that no sin or infirmity, which still remaineth against our will in us, can hinder us from being received of God in mercy, and from being made worthy partakers of this heavenly meat and drink.
author: Liturgy of Reformed Church
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Dear Lord! while we adoring pay 
 Our humble thanks to Thee, 
May every heart with rapture say, 
 "The Saviour died for me!"
author: Anne Steele
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: This bread and wine are the simple but eloquent monument to the infinite love of the Son of God, around which we gather with tender, tearful gratitude, because He loved us so, and because we know that our garlands of affection and consecration are pleasing to Him.
author: A. E. Kittredge
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Surely there is a fitness in the institution of the Lord's Supper as a standing memorial by which the church at large may commemorate the grandest act, and by which the heart of each individual believer may be reminded of his dearest friend. You, who have learned to love the Saviour, will prize His ordinance for the Saviour's sake. You who rejoice in the salvation purchased by His dying, will not fail with gratitude and faith to show the Lord's death until He come.
author: Wm. M. Punshon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Love and grief our hearts dividing, 
 With our tears His feet we bathe; 
Constant still, in faith abiding, 
 Life deriving from His death.
author: James Allen
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: To turn one's back on the memorial supper is to disregard the most tender and loving and melting of all our Saviour's commandments. It is not needful to know just how obedience will help us. It is enough to know that it was His dying command that we keep it till He come.
author: Henry M. Grout
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Attendance at the Lord's table is not a subject left to human choice; but to every disciple of Jesus His express and solemn command is, "Do this."
author: J. G. Pike
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Beloved, I congratulate you, that you are at the feast of redeeming love, that you know the riches of grace in Christ Jesus; but this is only the "early meal" (introductory feast); the "grand supper" is awaiting you, at the close of the day, in the palace of the King, where the fellowship will be perfect and eternal, where the table will be beyond all the mists and fogs of sin, where death never enters to disturb the festivities, and where we shall see the Lamb face to face. O! if the feast with Jesus here is so precious, what, what must heaven be!
author: A. E. Kittredge
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Brethren, here in the sacrament is the rainbow of the new and better covenant, the renewed pledge of salvation purchased, and strength imparted, and blessing conferred on the believing soul. And now, as in your covenant you pay your vows—time, talent, influence, property, life, all God's ,—He the Infinite, in boundless condescension stoops to whisper, "My light, my strength, my purity, my joy, my heaven, all yours." Thou hast avouched the Lord this day to be thy God, to walk in His ways, and to keep His statutes and His commandments, and His judgments, to hearken to His voice; and the Lord hath avouched thee this day to be His peculiar people, as He hath promised thee. And thus, brethren, in a mutual covenant of blessing, you do show forth His death until He come.
author: Wm. M. Punshon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: For they truly know their Lord in the breaking of bread, whose heart within them so vehemently burneth, whilst Thou, O blessed Jesus, dost walk and converse with them.
author: Thomas à Kempis
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We, too, must enter into the Saviour's sorrow. For us, if we believe in Him, He breaks the bread, and pours the wine; and when we eat and drink, we do show the Lord's death until He come. His death, not His life, though that was lustrous with a holiness without the shadow of a stain. His death, not His teaching, though that embodied the fullness of a wisdom that was Divine. His death, not His miracles, though His course was a march of mercy, and in His track of blessing the world rejoiced and was glad. His death! His body not glorious, but broken; His blood, not coursing through the veins of a conqueror, but shed, poured out for man. His death! Still His death! Grandest and most consecrating memory both for earth and heaven!
author: Wm. M. Punshon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We cannot embrace His cross, and yet refuse our own. We cannot raise the cup of His remembrance to our lips, without a secret pledge to Him, to one another, to the great company of the faithful in every age that we, too, hold ourselves at God's disposal, that we will ask nothing on our own account, that we will pass simply into the Divine hand to take us whither it will.
author: James Martineau
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Christ has given us, not only the ritual of an ordinance, but the pattern for our lives, when He took the cup, and gave thanks. So common joys become sacraments, enjoyment becomes worship, and the cup which holds the bitter or the sweet skillfully mingled for our lives becomes the cup of blessing and salvation drank in remembrance of Him.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Your participation of the holy communion must be regarded as the fresh act of your espousals, as the solemn renewal of your covenant; as your surrender, entire and unhesitating, to the service of the Lord. It is thus that you confess Christ, and witness of Him to the world. If you eat and drink without discerning this great purpose, you eat and drink unworthily; if you repudiate such purpose, either in thought or act, you crucify in your measure the Son of God afresh, and put Him to an open shame. By your profane use of the means of grace without the slightest desire for the grace of the means, it is as if you cut and wounded the Saviour in this the house of His friends, and sharpened the daggers of your treachery upon the tables of the violated law.
author: Wm. M. Punshon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The Lord's Supper! the marriage supper of the Lamb! There are vacant seats around the table here. Will there be dear ones missed at the table there?
author: A. E. Kittredge
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Of law there can be no less acknowledged than that her seat is the bosom of God, her voice the harmony of the world: all things in heaven and earth do her homage, the very least as feeling her care, and the greatest as not exempt from her power.
author: Richard Hooker
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The law of God is not the conflict of will with will, but of wisdom with folly, knowledge with ignorance, right with wrong—the announcement out of parental love , of the conditions of spiritual life, happiness, immortality. The punishment of sin, therefore, may be contemplated, not as the overflowing of wrath, but the outworkings of natural law, coincident with the judgment of infinite righteousness.
author: Edward Thomson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Laws, in their most general signification, are the necessary relations derived from the nature of things.
author: Montesquieu
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Law, meaning obedience to a holy God, passes by a natural transition into the gospel; that is, reverential duty to a person, to the obedience of love at last, which obeys, because the beautifulness of obedience is perceived.
author: F. W. Robertson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The law showed what man ought to be. Christ showed what man is, and what God is.
author: W. P. Mackay
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The law discovers the disease. The gospel gives the remedy.
author: Martin Luther
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The law is what we must do; the gospel what God will give.
author: Martin Luther
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The law sends us to Christ to be justified, and Christ sends us to the law to be regulated.
author: John Flavel
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Though the moral law has ceased as a covenant, it remains as a rule of life. It will forever continue as the standard of holiness.
author: Charles Backus
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The moral law is to be viewed not only as the rule of our obedience, but also as the reason of it. We must not only do what is commanded, and avoid what is forbidden in the law; but we must also do good, for this very reason, that God requires it, and avoid evil, because He forbids it.
author: Fisher's Catechism
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: A man may call himself a Christian—but the measure of his Christianity is the occupation of his mind and heart with the truth as it is in Jesus.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: In the school of Christ they are the best scholars who continue learning to the last.
author: Christian Scriver
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We cannot be scholars of Christ without trying to understand what is the place and the work in the world for which each of us is fitted. Every thing which befalls us is part of our education. Every event and condition of life is a lesson which is to be turned to account to make us more worthy of Him who by suffering was made perfect—who Himself entered not into glory, till first He had suffered pain.
author: Dean Stanley
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The disciples were not losing time when they sat beside their Master, and held quiet converse with Him under the olives of Bethany or by the shores of Galilee. Those were their school-hours; those were their feeding times.
author: T. L. Cuyler
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Brethren, we can rule our tempers, and we ought. Open the gospel, that most profound philosophy of the human soul, and yet most simple and practical directory of human duty; study it, fill your whole nature with its inspiration; set Christ before you; look upon His calm forehead and unstormed breast; think how He endured all contradiction of sinners, and endured them to the cross; and on the cross learn of Him then, for He was meek and lowly of heart.
author: Henry Giles
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Only, stay by his side 
 Till the page is really known, 
It may be we failed because we tried 
 To learn it all alone, 
And now that He would not let us lose 
 One lesson of love 
(For He knows the loss,)—can we refuse?
author: F. R. Havergal
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
A day, an hour of virtuous liberty, 
Is worth a whole eternity in bondage.
author: Addison
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The first freedom is freedom from sin.
author: Martin Luther
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There are two freedoms—the false, where a man is free to do what he likes; the true, where a man is free to do what he ought.
author: Charles Kingsley
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It is a question not often considered, whether we are not just as independent when we choose an upright and godly course, even if our fathers did walk in it, as when we follow somebody's example in sin. Indeed the highest and truest independence is that which always elects to do right.
author: Henry M. King
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Conquer thyself. Till thou hast done that, thou art a slave; for it is almost as well to be in subjection to another's appetite as thine own.
author: Burton
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The only rational liberty is that which is born of subjection, reared in the fear of God and the love of man, and made courageous in the defense of a trust and the prosecution of duty.
author: W. G. Simms
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Do you wish to be free? Then above all things, love God, love your neighbor, love one another, love the common weal; then you will have true liberty.
author: Savonarola
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: This is the true liberty of Christ, when a free man binds himself in love to duty. Not in shrinking from our distasteful occupations, but in fulfilling them, do we realize our high origin.
author: F. W. Robertson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The moment you accept God's ordering, that moment your work ceases to be a task, and becomes your calling; you pass from bondage to freedom, from the shadow-land of life Into life itself.
author: H. Clay Trumbull
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Not until right is founded upon reverence, will it be secure; not until duty is based upon love, will it be complete; not until liberty is based on eternal principles, will it be full, equal, lofty, and universal.
author: Henry Giles
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The great comprehensive truths, written on every page of our history, are these: Human happiness has no perfect security but freedom; freedom none but virtue; virtue none but knowledge; and neither freedom nor virtue has any vigor or immortal hope, except in the principles of the Christian faith, and in the sanctions of the Christian religion.
author: Quincy
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: What is liberty without wisdom and without virtue? It is the greatest of all possible evils, for it is folly, vice, and madness, without tuition or restraint.
author: Edmund Burke
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: That religion which holds that all men are equal in the sight of the great Father will not refuse to acknowledge that all citizens are equal in the sight of the law.
author: de Tocqueville
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Christianity is the companion of liberty in all its conflicts—the cradle of its infancy, and the Divine source of its claims.
author: de Tocqueville
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: True liberty can exist only when justice is equally administered to all.
author: Lord Mansfield
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The Spirit of God first imparts love; He next inspires hope, and then gives liberty; and that is about the last thing we have in a good many of our churches at the present time.
author: D. L. Moody
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: O, we all long for the day, the blessed day, when freedom shall at least be co-extensive with Christendom; when a slave political or domestic, shall not tread on an atom upon which the cross of Calvary has cast its shadow; when the baptism of the crucified shall be on every brow, the seal of a heavenly sonship; when the fire of a new Pentecost shall melt asunder, by its divine heat of charity, the bond which wrong or prejudice has fastened; when, to touch any spot over the wide sweep of God's Christianized earth, any spot which the gospel of the Saviour has ever visited, which the name of the Saviour has ever sanctified, shall be, in itself, the spell of a complete deliverance, the magic of a perfect franchise.
author: Henry Giles
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Illustrious confessors of Jesus Christ, a Christian finds in prison the same joys as the prophets tasted in the desert. Call it not a dungeon, but a solitude. When the soul is in heaven, the body feels not the weight of fetters; it carries the whole man along with it.
author: Tertullian
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Life as we call it, is nothing but the edge of the boundless ocean of existence when it comes upon soundings.
author: O. W. Holmes
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Life is before you,—not earthly life alone, but life —a thread running interminably through the warp of eternity.
author: J. G. Holland
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
O thou child of many prayers! 
Life hath quicksands, Life hath snares! 
Care and age come unawares!
author: Longfellow
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It is not possible to set out in the Christian profession with a more instructive or impressive idea than this— Life is the seed-time for eternity.
author: John Angel James
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The grand question of life is, Is my name written in heaven?
author: D. L. Moody
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The end of life is to be like unto God; and the soul following God, will be like unto Him.
author: Socrates
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: God help us! it is a foolish little thing, this human life, at the best; and it is half ridiculous and half pitiful to see what importance we ascribe to it, and to its little ornaments and distinctions.
author: Jeffrey
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There is no life so humble that, if it be true and genuinely human and obedient to God, it may not hope to shed some of His light. There is no life so meager that the greatest and wisest of us can afford to despise it. We cannot know at what moment it may flash forth with the life of God.
author: Phillips Brooks
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Life is rather a state of embryo, a preparation for life; a man is not completely born till he has passed through death.
author: Franklin
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: As one climbs a mountain roadway, and looks off on the landscape through the forest trees or from some overtopping crag, at each step he sees more and more of the outlying beauty of field and lake and forest and hill and river, till he reaches the summit, where the whole vast scene opens to the view, and enthuses his soul with delight. So life should be a constant lookout, through the gray mists, through the falling shadows, through the running tears, till he comes to the shining top of life in God Himself, where the fogs lift, and the shadows fall, and the view is all undisturbed.
author: T. B. Romeyn
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: A picture without sky has no glory. This present, unless we see gleaming beyond it the eternal calm of the heavens, above the tossing tree tops with withering leaves, and the smoky chimneys, is a poor thing for our eyes to gaze at, or our hearts to love, or our hands to toil on.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Life is great if properly viewed in any aspect; it is mainly great when viewed in connection with the world to come.
author: Albert Barnes
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There is no human life so poor and small as not to hold many a divine possibility.
author: James Martineau
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Life and religion are one, or neither is any thing.
author: George MacDonald
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Let the current of your being set towards God, then your life will be filled and calmed by one master-passion which unites and stills the soul.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Man's life is so interwoven with the grand life of his Maker that it admits of no adequate or rational interpretation except when the Creator as Supreme and the creatures of His hand as subordinate, are seen working in unison.
author: Charles H. Anthony
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: I believe that we cannot live better than in seeking to become better.
author: Socrates
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Making their lives a prayer.
author: Whittier
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: While we seek to fill up life in a way that will best secure the ends of our existence here, our whole plan and course of action should be such as will not hinder but serve our preparation for a future world.
author: Albert Barnes
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Pray for and work for fullness of life above every thing; full red blood in the body; full honesty and truth in the mind; and the fullness of a grateful love for the Saviour in your heart.
author: Phillips Brooks
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Every day that is born into the world comes .mw-parser-output .wst-tooltip{cursor:help;border-bottom:thin dotted cornflowerblue}.mw-parser-output .wst-tooltip-nodash{border-bottom:none} likes a burst of music, and rings itself all the way through; and thou shalt make of it a dance, a dirge, or a grand life-march as thou wilt.
author: Ladies' Repository
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Act as if you expected to live a hundred years, but might die to-morrow.
author: Ann Lee
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Nor love thy life, nor hate; but what thou livest, 
Live well; how long, or short, permit to Heaven.
author: Milton
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
We live in deeds, not years; in thoughts, not breaths; 
In feelings, not in figures on a dial. 
We should count time by heart-throbs. He most lives 
Who thinks most, feels the noblest, acts the best.
author: P. J. Bailey
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: I would not choose to go where I would be afraid to die, nor could I bear to live without a good hope for hereafter.
author: C. H. Spurgeon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Life is short, art long, opportunity fleeting, experiment uncertain, and judgment difficult.
author: Hippocrates
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: A few years hence and he will be beneath the sod; but those cliffs will stand, as now, facing the ocean, incessantly lashed by its waves, yet unshaken, immovable; and other eyes will gaze on them for their brief day of life, and then they, too, will close.
author: H. P. Liddon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: They waste life in what are called good resolutions—partial efforts at reformation, feebly commenced, heartlessly conducted, and hopelessly concluded.
author: Maturin
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It is infamy to die, and not be missed.
author: Carlos Wilcox
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: And thus does life go on, until death accomplishes the catastrophe in silence, takes the worn frame within his hand, and, as if it were a dried-up scroll, crumbles it in his grasp to ashes. The monuments of kingdoms, too, shall disappear. Still the globe shall move; still the stars shall burn; still the sun shall paint its colors on the day, and its colors on the year. What, then, is the individual, or what even is the race in the sublime recurrings of Time? Years, centuries, cycles, are nothing to these. The sun that measures out the ages of our planet is not a second-hand on the great dial of the universe.
author: Henry Giles
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Oh, I believe that there is no away; that no love, no life, goes ever from us; it goes as He went, that it may come again, deeper and closer and surer, and be with us always, even to the end of the world.
author: George MacDonald
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The highest life is a broken column; the fairest life, a tarnished gem; the richest life, an unripened fruit.
author: John Humpstone
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: This earth will be looked back on like a lowly home, and this life of ours be remembered like a short apprenticeship to duty.
author: Wm. Mountford
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: This is life's greatest moment, when the soul unfolds capacities which reach beyond earth's boundaries.
author: I. T. Hecker
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Life! we've been long together 
Through pleasant and through cloudy weather; 
 'Tis hard to part when friends are dear,— 
 Perhaps 'twill cost a sigh, a tear. 
 Then steal away, give little warning, 
 Choose thine own time, 
Say not "Good-night," but in some brighter clime, 
 Bid me "Good-morning."
author: A. L. Barbauld
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: A beautiful literature springs from the depth and fullness of intellectual and moral life, from an energy of thought and feeling, to which nothing, as we believe, ministers so largely as enlightened religion.
author: W. E. Channing
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: God be thanked for books! they are the voices of the distant and the dead, and make us heirs of the spiritual life of past ages. Books are the true levelers. They give to all who will faithfully use them the society, the spiritual presence, of the best and greatest of our race.
author: W. E. Channing
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: From the hour of the invention of printing, books, and not kings, were to rule the world. Weapons forged in the mind, keen-edged, and brighter than a sunbeam, were to supplant the sword and battle-axe. Books! lighthouses built on the sea of time! Books! by whose sorcery the whole pageantry of the world's history moves in solemn procession before our eyes. From their pages great souls look down in all their grandeur, undimmed by the faults and follies of earthly existence, consecrated by time.
author: E. P. Whipple
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Be less concerned about the number of books you read, and more about the good use you make of them. The best of books is the Bible.
author: Christian Scriver
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The great standard of literature as to purity and exactness of style is the Bible.
author: Blair
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Thou mayest as well expect to grow stronger by always eating, as wiser by always reading.
author: Fuller
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It is right for you, young men, to enrich yourselves with the spoils of all pure literature; but he who would make a favorite of a bad book, simply because it contains a few beautiful passages, might as well caress the hand of an assassin because of the jewelry which sparkles on his fingers.
author: Joseph Parker
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Love's secret is to be always doing things for God, and not to mind because they are such little ones.
author: F. W. Faber
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: At Toulon, Napoleon, looking out of the batteries, drew back a step to let some one take his place. The next moment the new arrived was killed. That step brought the French Empire, and made possible the bloody roll of its victories and defeats. The rout at Waterloo turned on a shower of rain hindering Grouchy's advance. The resolution of a moment, with some men, has been the turning-point of infinite issues to a world.
author: J. C. Geikie
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: One of the best things in the gospel of Jesus is the stress it lays on small things. It ascribes more value to quality than to quantity; it teaches that God does not ask how much we do, but how we do it.
author: J. F. Clarke
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Let us be content to do little, if God sets us at little tasks. It is but pride and self-will which says, "Give me something huge to fight,—and I should enjoy that—but why make me sweep the dust?"
author: Charles Kingsley
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Most people would succeed in small things if they were not troubled with great ambitions.
author: Longfellow
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The reason why those who are converted to Christ often make so poor a work of rectifying their old habits, is that they lay down their work in the very places where it needs to be prosecuted most carefully, that is, in their common employments. They do not live to God in that which is least.
author: Horace Bushnell
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: For honesty is before honor; and though man must write his poems in sounding words, God's poems are printed best in the brave and silent duties of common life.
author: Edward Garrett
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We are to work after no set fashion of high endeavor; but to walk with Jesus, performing, as it were, a ministry on foot, that we may stop at the humblest matter, and prove our fidelity there.
author: Horace Bushnell
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There are no trifles in the moral universe of God. Speak me a word to-day;—it shall go ringing on through the ages.
author: Wm. M. Punshon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: God, who prepares His work for the ages, accomplishes it by the feeblest instruments. It is the method of His providence to produce great results from inconsiderable means. The law which prevades the kingdom of nature is discerned in the history of mankind. Truth makes silent progress, like the water that trickles behind the rocks, and loosens them from the mountain on which they rest. Suddenly the hidden operation is revealed, and a single day suffices to lay bare the work of years, if not of ages.
author: John Lanahan
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Duty is duty, conscience is conscience, right is right, and wrong is wrong, whatever sized type they may be printed in. "Large" or "small" are not words for the vocabulary of conscience.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: If we would gain light either on the theory or the practice of religion: 1. We must sincerely desire the light. 2. We must use the light we already have. 3. We must patiently seek light in the double way of prayer and rational inquiry. Never, as long as the world stands, will any religiously benighted soul thus patiently desire and pray and labor for the break of day, without at last seeing the eyelids of the morn unsealed, and the painfully dusky east gradually redden into the sun.
author: E. F. Burr
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: That soul is on the certain path toward light which, sincerely desiring the light, constantly submits to the claims of the light as they are made known. That soul cannot stay in darkness, any more than a flower opening its petals broadly to the sun can stay in shadow.
author: Wayland Hoyt
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There is no long interval between the sense of thirst and the trickling of the stream over the parched lip; but ever it is flowing, flowing past us, and the desire is but the opening of the lips to receive the limpid, and life-giving waters. No one ever desired the grace of God, really and truly desired it, but just in proportion as he desired it, he got it; just in proportion as he thirsted, he was satisfied.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The soul that rightly receives Christ is in a longing condition; never did the hart pant for the water brooks, never did the hireling desire the shadow, never did a condemned person long for a pardon more than the soul longs for Christ.
author: John Flavel
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: A living man must have a living God, or his soul will perish in the midst of earthly plenty, and will thirst and die whilst the water of earthly delights is running all around him. We are made to need persons not things .
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Our yearnings are homesicknesses for heaven; our sighings are for God, just as children that cry themselves asleep away from home, and sob in their slumber, know not that they sob for their parents. The soul's inarticulate moanings are the affections yearning for the Infinite, and having no one to tell them what it is that ails them.
author: H. W. Beecher
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Come! for I need Thy love, 
 More than the flower the dew, or grass the rain; 
Come like Thy Holy Dove, 
 And let me in Thy sight rejoice to live again.
author: Jones Very
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: My friends, look to Christ, and not to yourselves. That is what is the matter with a great many sinners; instead of looking to Christ, they are looking at the bite of sin.
author: D. L. Moody
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: One of Satan's devices to keep poor souls in a sad, doubting, and questioning condition is causing them to be always posing and musing upon sin; to mind their sins more than their Saviour: yea, so to mind their sins as to forget and neglect their Saviour. Their eyes are so fixed upon their disease that they cannot see their remedy, though it be near; and they do so muse upon their debts that they have neither mind nor heart to think of their surety.
author: Thomas Brooks
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: How can we in practice copy Jesus? How do you write a copy in your copy-book? By constantly looking at the top line, imitating its capital letters, small letters, up-strokes, downstrokes, even stops . So be always "looking unto Jesus."
author: Eugene Stock
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Love is the emblem of eternity; it confounds all notion of time; effaces all memory of a beginning, all fear of an end.
author: Madame de Staël
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: It is love that asks, that seeks, that knocks, that finds, and that is faithful to what it finds.
author: St. Augustine
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Love is the greatest thing that God can give us, for Himself is love; and it is the greatest thing we can give to God, for it will also give ourselves, and carry with it all that is ours.
author: Jeremy Taylor
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Love is the crowning grace of humanity, the holiest right of the soul, the golden link which binds us to duty and truth, the redeeming principle that chiefly reconciles the heart to life, and is prophetic of eternal good.
author: Petrarch
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Love is a passion 
Which kindles honor into noble acts.
author: Dryden
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

author: Young
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Love reflects the thing beloved.
author: Tennyson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Affection is the broadest basis of a good life.
author: George Eliot
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Heaven's harmony is universal love.
author: Cowper
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Of the systems above us, angelic and seraphic, we know little; but we see one law, simple, efficient, and comprehensive as that of gravitation,—the law of love,—extending its sway over the whole of God's dominions, living where He lives, embracing every moral movement in its universal authority, and producing the same harmony, where it is obeyed as we observe in the movements of nature.
author: Mark Hopkins
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The love that gushes for all is the real elixir of life—the fountain of bodily longevity. It is the lack of this that always produces the feeling of age.
author: J. G. Holland
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: God be thanked that there are some in the world to whose hearts the barnacles will not cling.
author: J. G. Holland
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The incarnation of God in Christ reveals this truth, that the love that seeks and saves the lost is a love that suffers. On the one side there is loss, Gethsemane and the rugged burden of Golgotha, but on the other is gain, the gain of a world's redemption.
author: Wesley R. Davis
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: If there is any thing that keeps the mind open to angel visits, and repels the ministry of ill, it is human love.
author: N. P. Willis
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Love would master self; and having made the mastery stretch onward and upward toward infinitude.
author: Donald G. Mitchell
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Learn the new commandment of the Son of God. Not to love merely, but to love as He loved . Go forth in this spirit to your life-duties; go forth,—children of the cross, to carry every thing before you, and win victories for God by the conquering power of a love like His.
author: F. W. Robertson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Ah, how skillful grows the hand 
That obeyeth Love's command! 
It is the heart, and not the brain, 
That to the highest doth attain, 
And he who followeth Love's behest 
 Far excelleth all the rest!
author: Longfellow
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The most beautiful sight this earth affords is a man or woman so filled with love that duty is only a name, and its performance the natural outflow and expression of the love which has become the central principle of their life.
author: J. G. Holland
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Be loving, and you will never want for love; be humble, and you will never want for guiding.
author: D. M. Craik
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: I have often had occasion to observe, that a warm blundering man does more for the world than a frigid wise man.
author: Richard Cecil
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Charity is the very livery of Christ.
author: Latimer
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Love is a golden key to let in Christ, and a strong lock to keep out others.
author: Thomas Brooks
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Divine love is a sacred flower, which in its early bud is happiness, and in its full bloom is heaven.
author: E. L. Hervey
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Christ is not valued at all unless He be valued above all.
author: St. Augustine
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The true measure of loving God is to love Him without measure.
author: St. Bernard
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Between God and man, between the gospel and each soul, the interpreter is Love.
author: Vinet
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: God is all love, and the more we are like Him the more we shall love; the trouble is not in the quantity but the quality of our love. If it were wholly pure, wholly unselfish, it could not be too deep or intense; for all true loving lifts us to a higher plane, bringing us nearer to God and the eternal good.
author: A. H. K
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: To be like Christ in His love is far more than to be like Him in His knowlege, if we were forced to choose between them; but they harmonize and strengthen each other; more knowledge will help us to love more; and more love help us to know more.
author: A. H. K
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Love is the active, working principle in all true faith. It is its very soul, without which it is dead. "Faith works by love."
author: Jonathan Edwards
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: But how shall this love be demonstrated? After what method shall it be expressed? Not by secret musings alone; not by the chanting of religious sonnets alone; not by grateful remembrances of Him—at His table only—but by deeds of love towards those who in a real sense represent Him, because partakers of that nature, our common humanity, which He condescended to assume.
author: William Adams
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Consider that as a principle of love is the main principle in the heart of a real Christian, so the labor of love, is the main business of the Christian life.
author: Jonathan Edwards
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: True love goes ever straight forward, not in its own strength, but esteeming itself as nothing. Then indeed we are truly happy. The cross is no longer a cross when there is no self to suffer under it.
author: Fenelon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: A mightier love for the Son of God, to overpower and subdue and lead captive these wayward and truant affections of the natural heart—this is what is needed.
author: A. J. Gordon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: All true love to God is preceded in the heart by these two things—a sense of sin, and an assurance of pardon. There is no love possible—real, deep, genuine, worthy of being called love of God—which does not start with the belief of my own transgression, and with the thankful reception of forgiveness in Christ.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The disciple whom Jesus loved leaned on His bosom. Dear friend, where are you?
author: Anna Shipton
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Her heart was a passion-flower, bearing within it the crown of thorns and the cross of Christ.
author: Jeremy Taylor
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Dear Saviour! we are Thine, 
 By everlasting bands; 
Our hearts, our souls, we would resign 
 Entirely to Thy hands.
author: Doddridge
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Love Christ, and then the eternity in the heart will not be a great aching void, but will be filled with the everlasting life which Christ gives and is.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Give me a baptism of glowing love, 
Thy power and presence wheresoe'er I rove; 
And my last prayer, all other prayers above 
 Oh, give to me 
More of Thyself, Lord Jesus: more of Thee!
author: Anna Shipton
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Lord, thou knowest all things; Thou knowest that I love Thee!
author: Bible
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Let us learn how the love of Christ, received into the heart, triumphs gradually but surely over all sin, transforms character, turning even its weakness into strength, and so, from the depths of transgression and the very gates of hell, raises men to God.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

author: St. Bernard
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Christ is not sweet till sin be made bitter to us.
author: John Flavel
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Lovest thou me? This is the one test question of our religion—for he that loveth is born of God.
author: William Adams
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

author: F. R. Havergal
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: No man loveth God except the man who has first learned that God loves him.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
For they the mind of Christ discern 
Who lean, like John, upon His breast.
author: J. G. Whittier
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
How shall we test our love? 
 How shall the real be known 
From that which takes its form? 
 Love "seeketh not her own."
author: Mrs. M. F. Butts
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: None know how to prize the Saviour, but such as are zealous in pious works for others.
author: Lady Huntingdon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Earthly joy can take but a bat-like flight, always checked, always limited, in dusk and darkness. But the love of Christ breaks through the vaulting, and leads us up into the free sky above, expanding to the very throne of Jehovah, and drawing us still upward to the infinite heights of glory.
author: F. R. Havergal
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

author: Horatius Bonar
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Pure love is in the will alone; it is no sentimental love, for the imagination has no part in it; it loves, if we may so express it, without feeling, as faith believes without seeing.
author: Fenelon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Love is the foundation of all obedience. Without it morality degenerates into mere casuistry. Love is the foundation of all knowledge. Without it religion degenerates into a chattering about Moses and doctrines and theories; a thing that will neither kill nor make alive, that never gave life to a single soul or blessing to a single heart, and never put strength into any hand in the conflict and strife of daily life.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Mourning after an absent God is an evidence of a love as strong, as rejoicing in a present one.
author: F. W. Robertson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
Oh! make me Thine forever; 
 And should I fainting be, 
Lord! let me never, never, 
 Outlive my love to Thee!
author: Gerhardt
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: When a man is told that the whole of religion and morality is summed up in the two commandments, to love God, and to love our neighbor, he is ready to cry, like Charoba in Gebir, at the first sight of the sea, "Is this the mighty ocean? is this all?" Yes, all; but how small a part of it do your eyes survey! Only trust yourself to it; launch out upon it; sail abroad over it; you will find it has no end; it will carry you round the world.
author: Guesses at Truth
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Apart from the positive woes of perdition, an eternity of wretchedness grows from the want of love to Christ as naturally as the oak grows from the acorn, or the harvest from the scattered grain. It is not that love to Christ merits heaven; it does far better, it makes heaven. It is, as it were, the organ of sensation that takes note of heaven's blessedness.
author: A. H. Boyd
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Nothing satisfies God but the voluntary sacrifice of love. The pain of Christ gave God no pleasure—only the love that was tested by pain—the love of perfect obedience.
author: F. W. Robertson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: How shall I do to love? Believe. How shall I do to believe? Love.
author: Leighton
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: We are strangers to Christian love, if we harbor malice or revenge in our hearts toward any of our fellow-creatures, whatever treatment we receive at their hands.
author: Charles Backus
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: To be useful as a Christian, a man must keep himself free from all malign feelings, from all bitterness of resentment. Even righteous indignation must not drag Love from her throne. Over all the soul's passions Love must preside in serene majesty. The Christian worker must learn (and the sooner the better) if he has not already learned, that there is something better for a Christian than to plan revenge, and nurse resentment, and call down fire from heaven, even on those who show themselves base and unworthy.
author: Prof. Ballard
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Beware of that which becomes the slanderer's life, of magnifying every speck of evil and closing the eye to goodness, till at last men arrive at the state in which generous, universal love (which is heaven) becomes impossible, and a suspicious, universal hate takes possession of the heart, and that is hell.
author: F. W. Robertson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There is no cure for ossification of the heart. Oh, that miserable state, when to the jaundiced eye all good transforms itself into evil, and the very instruments of health become the poison of disease.
author: F. W. Robertson
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Man is the crowning of history and the realization of poetry, the free and living bond which unites all nature to that God who created it for Himself.
author: F. Godet
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Let us not undervalue the dignity of human nature. Man, although fallen, still retains some traces of his primeval glory and excellence—broken columns of a celestial temple, magnificent, even in its ruins.
author: John McC. Holmes
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote:
How poor, how rich, how abject, how august, 
How complicate, how wonderful is man!
author: Young
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The older I grow—and I now stand upon the brink of eternity—the more comes back to me that sentence in the Catechism which I learned when a child, and the fuller and deeper its meaning becomes, "What is the chief end of man? To glorify God and enjoy Him forever."
author: Thomas Carlyle
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: What a chimera is man! what a confused chaos! what a subject of contradiction! a professed judge of all things, and yet a feeble worm of the earth! the great depositary and guardian of truth, and yet a mere huddle of uncertainty! the glory and the scandal of the universe!
author: Pascal
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Man has wants deeper than can be supplied by wealth or nature or domestic affections. His great relations are to his God and to eternity.
author: Mark Hopkins
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: In that vast march, the van forgets the rear; the individual is lost; and yet the multitude is many individuals. He faints and falls and dies; man is forgotten; but still mankind move on, still worlds revolve, and the will of God is done in earth and heaven.
author: G. W. Curtis
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The Divine government of the world is like a stream that rolls under us; men are only as bubbles that rise on its surface; some are brighter and larger, and sparkle longer in the sun than others; but all must break; whilst the mighty current rolls on in its wonted majesty!
author: David Thomas
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: But if, indeed, there be a nobler life in us than in these strangely moving atoms; if, indeed, there is an eternal difference between the fire which inhabits them, and that which animates us,—it must be shown, by each of us in his appointed place, not merely in the patience, but in the activity of our hope, not merely by our desire, but our labor, for the time when the dust of the generations of men shall be confirmed for foundations of the gates of the city of God.
author: John Ruskin
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Power in its measure and degree is the measure of manhood.
author: J. G. Holland
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Give us an age in which Christian manhood shall assert itself as the highest earthly thing and the noblest earthly estate. Give us an age that, instead of whining and groaning under the truth, shall rejoice in the truth. Give us an age which, lifted into identity with its highest possessions, shall be made by those possessions patient, pure, heroic, and honorable.
author: J. G. Holland
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: Obedience, submission, discipline, courage—these are among the characteristics which make a man.
author: Samuel Smiles
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The man, whom I call deserving the name, is one whose thoughts and exertions are for others rather than himself.
author: Walter Scott
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The finest fruit earth holds up to its Maker is a finished man .
author: Humboldt
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: A Christian is the gentlest of men; but then he is a man.
author: C. H. Spurgeon
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: There is a great deal more correctness of thought respecting manhood in bodily things than in moral things. For men's ideas of manhood shape themselves as the tower and spire of cathedrals do, that stand broad at the bottom, but grow tapering as they rise, and end, far up, in the finest lines, and in an evanishing point. Where they touch the ground they are most, and where they reach to the heaven they are least.
author: H. W. Beecher
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: I long to have the children feel that there is nothing in this world more attractive, more earnestly to be desired than manhood in Jesus Christ.
author: H. W. Beecher
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The manliness of Christian love, and the putting away from ourselves of all fear, because we are "perfected in love," is one of the highest lessons that the gospel teaches us, and one of the greatest things which the gospel gives us.
author: Alexander Maclaren
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: The conscience of every man recognizes courage as the foundation of manliness, and manliness as the perfection of human character.
author: Thomas Hughes
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: In proportion as man gets back the spirit of manliness, which is self-sacrifice, affection, loyalty to an idea beyond himself, a God above himself, so far will he rise above circumstances, and wield them at his will.
author: Charles Kingsley
sourceName: Three Thousand Selected Quotations from Brilliant Writers — Wikisource

quote: "The work of men"—and what is that? Well, we may any of us know very quickly, on the condition of being wholly ready to do it.
